title: Warm up the registers
prompt:
Three values arrive on input, and the starter has already read them into the registers `a_r`, `b_r`, and `c_r`. Compute `(a + b) - c` and print it.

The starter prints whatever the result register holds, so all that is missing is the arithmetic in the middle. Two instructions are enough.

## what is checked

- the combined result is printed on its own line
- the program exits cleanly
- the subtraction actually happens (no writing the answer in directly)
- the same holds for other inputs you do not see, zero and negative values among them
starter:
// combine three values into one result and print it
define(fp, x29)
define(lr, x30)

define(result_r, x19)
define(a_r, x20)
define(b_r, x21)
define(c_r, x22)

        .data
fmt_in:     .string "%lld %lld %lld"
fmt_out:    .string "result = %lld\n"

        .bss
        .balign 8
a_m:        .skip 8
b_m:        .skip 8
c_m:        .skip 8

        .text
        .balign 4
        .global main
main:
        stp     fp, lr, [sp, -16]!
        mov     fp, sp

        ldr     x0, =fmt_in                 // read a, b, and c
        ldr     x1, =a_m
        ldr     x2, =b_m
        ldr     x3, =c_m
        bl      scanf
        ldr     x9, =a_m
        ldr     a_r, [x9]
        ldr     x9, =b_m
        ldr     b_r, [x9]
        ldr     x9, =c_m
        ldr     c_r, [x9]                   // the deduction
        mov     result_r, 0                 // replace this placeholder

        // TODO: compute (a + b) - c into result_r

        ldr     x0, =fmt_out
        mov     x1, result_r
        bl      printf

        mov     w0, 0
        ldp     fp, lr, [sp], 16
        ret
